text.arabic_uthmani: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِۦ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ ۖ فَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that both resumes the prior discourse and launches a general sending principle
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa-}}) opens the ayah by carrying the prior warning (14:3) into a new rule about divine communication. The immediate move into the negated restriction frame lets continuity and a fresh axiom arrive together: the discourse has not left the earlier problem, but it now explains it through prophetic sending.

topics.headline: resumptive opening into a sending rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as both continuation and new principle, so the language rule answers the previous condition rather than floating alone.
topics.reason: The opening connector precedes the negated sending formula, and the clause evidence marks a new restricted sending statement linked to the prior discourse.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening an exclusive restriction: no sending case remains outside the stated exception
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) does not make a simple denial. It opens a long negation that waits for the exception particle, so the reader hears the rule form before the content of the exception appears: no messenger-sending falls outside the local-language condition.

topics.headline: negation that waits for exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah forming an exceptionless rule, not merely reporting that something did not happen.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar identifies the negation-exception construction, and the clause extends from the negator through the exception phrase.

words.gloss_range: settled divine sending or dispatch inside the universal restriction; active, deliberate, and agent-marked
words.root_gloss_range: root range of sending, dispatching, release, flow, and messenger-family language; local Form IV selects commissioned divine dispatch while retaining controlled-release pressure
words.prose: {{ar:أَرْسَلْنَا}} ({{tr:arsalnā}}) is the first lexical action of the ayah, and its perfect first-person plural form makes the sending rule sound like established divine practice. The Form IV shape turns any release-image in {{ar:ر س ل}} ({{tr:r-s-l}}) into commissioned dispatch, while the nearby messenger noun makes the act and office answer each other. The same root also starts a Surah 14 messenger thread that is immediately instantiated with Moses (14:5).

topics.headline: settled divine dispatch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rule is spoken as established divine practice by the divine speaker, not as an agentless historical pattern.
topics.reason: The perfect Form IV verb carries a first-person plural subject and governs the messenger object inside the restriction frame.

topics.headline: release disciplined into commissioning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the sending root as dispatch rather than uncontrolled release, because the local derived form disciplines the root image into commissioned mission.
topics.reason: The root family includes release-like pressure, but local Form IV and transitive syntax select deliberate commissioned sending.

topics.headline: root reprise and surah mission thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sending verb as the start of a repeated mission thread, with the adjacent messenger noun and the next ayah (14:5) reinforcing the same root field.
topics.reason: The contextual rows link this root to later Surah 14 messenger scenes and to the adjacent same-root object.

words.gloss_range: emphatic preposition after negation that exhausts the messenger class: not even one messenger outside the exception
words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) strengthens the negative class rather than adding a normal spatial phrase. In the slot before the indefinite messenger noun, it makes the rule cover every possible member of the messenger class before the exception restores the one valid mode.

topics.headline: exhaustive class marker after negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the restriction is universalized down to any single messenger, not stated as a loose generalization.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the preposition as governing the messenger noun in a negative context that reinforces universality.

words.gloss_range: indefinite singular messenger as a class term under negation; a sent person whose office carries communication
words.root_gloss_range: root range of sending, dispatch, messengerhood, and message-bearing; local noun selects the sent human office with communicative metonymy active

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: settled divine dispatch in the same sending-root frame

words.prose: {{ar:رَّسُولٍ}} ({{tr:rasūlin}}) is singular, indefinite, and governed by the emphatic particle, so one messenger stands for the entire office. Its same-root relation to {{ar:أَرْسَلْنَا}} ({{tr:arsalnā}}) makes the wording hear like sent no sent-one, and the noun keeps person and message close: the dispatched human is the carrier of intelligible communication.

topics.headline: any messenger as a class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rule covers the prophetic office as a class rather than one named prophet.
topics.reason: The noun is singular indefinite and genitive under the negative construction, producing class-wide coverage.

topics.headline: messenger as person and message carrier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that messengerhood is communicative office: the sent person and the message he carries cannot be separated in the local language rule.
topics.reason: The lexical rows support metonymic person-message pressure, while local grammar still selects a human messenger noun.

topics.headline: same-root echo with the sending verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the sending act repeated in the messenger noun and sees that root field continue into later Surah 14 messenger scenes.
topics.reason: The adjacent verb and object share the sending root, and the surah profile traces later messenger references.

words.gloss_range: exception particle that flips universal negation into exclusive affirmation of the language condition
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) is the pivot of the first beat. Everything before it exhausts the possibility of messenger-sending outside the rule; everything after it names the one permitted mode, the people's own tongue.

topics.headline: polarity pivot of the restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact turning point where denial becomes exclusive affirmation.
topics.reason: The particle completes the negation-exception construction and introduces the modal exception phrase.

words.gloss_range: preposition making the tongue the means or medium of sending, governing the whole possessed-language phrase
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) makes language the medium of the exception. It can be heard as tool and communicative space at once, and its attachment to the tongue noun binds the following construct chain into one compact modal phrase.

topics.headline: language as tool and medium
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the people's tongue is not an ornament of the messenger but the means and environment of communication.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the tongue noun after the exception and licenses an instrumental or modal reading.

topics.headline: single preposition over the whole chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole language phrase held together as the single surviving condition in the restriction.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows the preposition governing the construct phrase headed by the tongue noun.

words.gloss_range: possessed communal tongue or language, both embodied speech and intelligible medium; singular locally but able to bear communal plurality
words.root_gloss_range: root range of tongue, speech, language, articulate expression, eloquence, and representative mouthpiece; local construct selects the people’s intelligible speech-medium
words.prose: {{ar:لِسَانِ}} ({{tr:lisāni}}) is the center of the exception phrase: governed by the preposition and governing the people noun. The construct makes language a communal possession, while {{ar:ل س ن}} ({{tr:l-s-n}}) keeps the physical tongue, speech, eloquence, and representative voice together. Variant pressure can expose plurality inside the community, but the local singular construct still names the shared communicative medium; the clear-tongue formula at 26:195 becomes one instance of this wider rule.

topics.headline: construct head of the exception phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices language as something possessed by a people, not a free-floating code chosen outside them.
topics.reason: The word is governed by the preposition and governs the people noun as construct head.

topics.headline: embodied tongue and articulate voice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the language rule keeps embodied speech and representative articulation alive, while local grammar still selects the language medium rather than a literal organ alone.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports tongue, speech, eloquence, and spokesperson pressure; the local phrase narrows these to intelligible communal language.

topics.headline: singular phrase with plural pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one tongue can carry communal diversity, while the canonical local surface remains singular in construct.
topics.reason: Variant rows expose compressed or plural tongue forms without replacing the aligned singular construct in the local reading.

topics.headline: universal rule behind a clear-tongue instance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the language phrase as part of the messenger-clarification field, with the clear Arabic tongue scene (26:195) functioning as a concrete instance of the rule.
topics.reason: The contextual rows connect tongue, messenger, and clarification fields, and the intertext row supplies the concrete 26:195 instance.

words.gloss_range: possessed collective people: the messenger’s own community as source of the tongue and recipient of clarification
words.root_gloss_range: root range of standing, rising, maintaining, establishing, and constituted peoplehood; local noun selects a collective community bound to its messenger
words.prose: {{ar:قَوْمِهِ}} ({{tr:qawmihī}}) completes the construct chain by saying whose tongue it is. The suffix binds each messenger to his own people, and the singular collective treats many hearers as one communicative body. The {{ar:ق و م}} ({{tr:q-w-m}}) standing-field makes the people a constituted community, not a random crowd, and the general rule is immediately concretized with Moses and his people (14:5).

topics.headline: his own people as language source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that universality is achieved through many local messenger-people bonds, not by bypassing local communities.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix refers back to the messenger noun and completes the construct phrase.

topics.headline: people as a standing collective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the audience as an established collective with shared standing, while the local sense remains people or community.
topics.reason: The root field supports standing and establishment pressure, but the local noun selects the collective community.

topics.headline: general people-rule becomes a Moses scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the general phrase prepare the next ayah, where Moses is sent to his people (14:5).
topics.reason: The contextual and echo rows connect this people noun to repeated Surah 14 people scenes, especially 14:5.

words.gloss_range: purpose particle that turns local-language sending toward clarification
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li-}}) pivots from the exception phrase to its purpose. The language rule is not bare accommodation; it exists so that clarification can happen for the people.

topics.headline: purpose hinge into clarification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices why the local tongue matters: it is grammatically ordered toward making things clear.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as purposive and the attachment evidence makes the following verb the purpose clause of sending.

words.gloss_range: purpose-governed Form II clarification: the messenger actively makes distinctions clear for the people, with the object left broad
words.root_gloss_range: root range of between-ness, separation, becoming clear, making clear, evidence, and distinctness; local Form II selects active clarifying that differentiates
words.prose: {{ar:يُبَيِّنَ}} ({{tr:yubayyina}}) states the purpose of local-language sending. Its hidden subject returns to the messenger, so clarification is delegated before the explicit divine subject takes over the outcome verbs. The omitted object keeps the scope broad, and {{ar:ب ي ن}} ({{tr:b-y-n}}) makes clarity an act of distinction; this is why the later split into misguidance and guidance comes after explanation, not before it.

topics.headline: messenger actively clarifies
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the messenger is assigned active clarification as the purpose of being sent.
topics.reason: The purposive particle governs the subjunctive Form II verb, whose implied subject is the messenger.

topics.headline: object left broad
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is clarified is left capacious: message, signs, path, and distinction can all be heard without a single object closing the frame.
topics.reason: The verb is transitive in force but has no explicit object in the local clause.

topics.headline: clarity as making distinctions visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that clarification is not just explanation; it separates what had been blurred or bent.
topics.reason: The root evidence joins clarity with separation and between-ness, matching the following divided outcome.

topics.headline: clarification precedes divided outcomes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the theological tension: universal clarity is the precondition, but it does not determine guidance.
topics.reason: The purpose clause precedes the result clause, and the boundary rows connect clarification to the prior crookedness problem and later outcome split.

words.gloss_range: benefactive or directional preposition marking the people as recipients of clarification
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la-}}) turns the people into the target-beneficiaries of clarification. Its closeness to the earlier purpose particle creates a small formal mirror: one particle marks why clarification happens, the other marks for whom it happens.

topics.headline: clarification directed for them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that clarification is aimed at the people’s reception, not merely uttered near them.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the plural pronoun and marks the beneficiary or target of the clarification verb.

topics.headline: two close particles with different roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the formal repetition of the particle while its function changes from purpose to beneficiary.
topics.reason: The two nearby particles have distinct syntactic functions in the purpose clause.

words.gloss_range: attached plural pronoun referring back to the people as actual recipients of clarification
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) resumes the possessed people as plural recipients. The singular collective people who supplied the tongue now become the actual hearers for whom clarification is performed, closing the purpose beat before the outcome hinge.

topics.headline: people become plural recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the communicative loop: the people provide the tongue and then receive clarification through it.
topics.reason: The referent profile links the pronoun back to the people noun, and its position closes the purpose clause before the following result particle.

words.gloss_range: result or sequence connector moving from messenger clarification to divine outcome
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) is the ayah’s central hinge. It allows result and sequence pressure together: after the messenger clarifies, the scene turns to divine allocation of misguidance and guidance. That makes the paradox structural rather than incidental, especially against the resistant backdrop from 14:3.

topics.headline: after clarification comes divine outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the agency shift from messenger clarification to divine outcome without losing sequence.
topics.reason: The connector introduces the result clause after the purpose clause and attaches directly to the misguidance verb.

topics.headline: clarity does not guarantee guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the startling order: clarified speech can be followed by misguidance before guidance is named.
topics.reason: The central connector places misguidance after clarification, producing the ayah’s tension.

topics.headline: prior resistance makes the consequence legible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the result hinge is not arbitrary because the prior ayah has already profiled obstruction and crookedness.
topics.reason: The boundary evidence links the result clause to the resistance described immediately before 14:4.

words.gloss_range: ongoing causative misguiding of an open human object, first pole of the will-governed outcome binary after clarification
words.root_gloss_range: root range of straying, losing the way, being hidden or vanished from perception; local Form IV selects causing someone to stray while retaining lost-access pressure
words.prose: {{ar:يُضِلُّ}} ({{tr:yuḍillu}}) names the first outcome after clarification, and its Form IV shape makes misguidance causative and object-affecting. The {{ar:ض ل ل}} ({{tr:ḍ-l-l}}) field adds lostness and hiddenness to wrong direction, while the order places this negative pole before guidance. The root also reopens the straying state from 14:3 and later narrows toward wrongdoers in 14:27.

topics.headline: causing to stray as an ongoing act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misguidance is not merely self-straying here; it is a divine causative act applied to an object.
topics.reason: The Form IV imperfect verb takes the following open relative as object and is later supplied with the divine subject.

topics.headline: straying as loss of access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels misguidance as becoming lost or unavailable to the clarified path, while the local verb still selects causing to stray.
topics.reason: The root evidence includes hiddenness and lostness, but local morphology selects causative misguidance.

topics.headline: negative pole named before guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shock that misguidance is named first after universal clarification.
topics.reason: The verb is coordinated with the guidance verb under the same subject, and the supplied rows mark their ordered binary.

topics.headline: prior straying becomes divine action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the previous straying state converted into divine causation here, with later Surah 14 specifying wrongdoers (14:27).
topics.reason: The echo rows connect 14:3, 14:4, and 14:27 through the same root field.

words.gloss_range: explicit divine proper-name subject centered between the two opposed outcome verbs
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name root field associated with deity, worship-orientation, and awe or bewilderment; local proper noun identifies the sovereign agent
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) is placed where the two opposed outcomes meet. It is the explicit nominative subject of misguiding and also governs the coordinated guidance verb, so neither outcome is agentless or assigned elsewhere. The proper name makes the binary a matter of divine agency, and the closing attributes will explain that agency as might joined to wisdom.

topics.headline: one divine subject for both verbs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both misguidance and guidance share one explicit subject.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the proper noun as the subject of the first outcome verb and shared subject of the coordinated second verb.

topics.headline: proper name with worship and awe pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the agent is the named God, with worship and awe pressure fitting the difficult pairing of opposed outcomes.
topics.reason: The derivational rows are valid pressure around the proper name, but local grammar selects the divine proper noun as subject.

topics.headline: action hinge later sealed by attributes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the shift from human obstruction in 14:3 to divine governance, with the later attribute seal explaining the same actor.
topics.reason: The contextual rows place the divine name at the center of sending, will, misguidance, guidance, and attribute fields.

words.gloss_range: open relative object of misguidance: whomever, defined by divine will rather than a named criterion
words.prose: {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the human recipient slot for misguidance without naming a class. Its force is open and relative, and it prepares the identical phrase that will return in the guidance half, so the two outcomes differ by verb, not by object grammar.

topics.headline: open recipient slot for the first outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the misled class is grammatically open and will be mirrored exactly in the guidance clause.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is object of the misguidance verb and begins the phrase repeated for the guidance outcome.

words.gloss_range: ongoing divine willing whose understood object is the misguidance outcome; criteria are unstated and the phrase prepares exact repetition
words.root_gloss_range: root range of willing, determining, and thingness or bringing-about; local Form I selects divine willing with outcome-specifying pressure
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَاءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) supplies the will clause for the first open recipient. Its object is understood from the misguidance outcome, so the willing is not empty, but the criteria are withheld. The {{ar:ش ي أ}} ({{tr:sh-y-ʾ}}) field lets will feel like determination of an outcome, and the same form will return unchanged for guidance.

topics.headline: ongoing will tied to the outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices divine willing as ongoing and outcome-directed, not a detached mood statement.
topics.reason: The imperfect will verb completes the relative clause and its understood object is supplied by the misguidance clause.

topics.headline: will as determination pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses will as specification that brings an outcome into determination, while local grammar still selects the will verb.
topics.reason: The root evidence links willing and thingness, but the local surface is the Form I will verb.

topics.headline: criteria withheld in a repeated formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that selection criteria are deliberately absent and that the exact formula will balance both outcomes.
topics.reason: The same will phrase recurs at words 21-22 and the rows identify the repeated architecture and opacity.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector that makes guidance the parallel second act in the outcome binary
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa-}}) coordinates guidance with misguidance as a matched divine act. It prevents the second verb from feeling like an afterthought or subordinate correction; the two outcomes stand side by side under one subject.

topics.headline: guidance coordinated with misguidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the two opposite outcomes as a balanced pair rather than a loose sequence.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the guidance verb with the misguidance verb under the same divine subject.

words.gloss_range: direct divine guiding of an open human object, positive pole of the outcome binary under the same will formula
words.root_gloss_range: root range of guidance, leading, direction, gift, offering, and conveyed alignment; local Form I selects direct divine guiding with benefactive gift-pressure
words.prose: {{ar:يَهْدِي}} ({{tr:yahdī}}) completes the divine outcome pair as direct guidance of an open recipient. The {{ar:ه د ي}} ({{tr:h-d-y}}) field gives direction a granted or conveyed feel, while local grammar keeps guidance rather than a literal gift as the selected sense. Its Form I shape contrasts with the causative misguidance verb, and the root continues through later Surah 14 guidance claims (14:12; 14:21).

topics.headline: direct guidance of another
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices guidance as divine leading of a recipient, not autonomous self-guidance.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb is coordinated with the prior outcome verb and takes the following open relative as object.

topics.headline: guidance felt as bestowed direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels guidance as directed alignment granted by God, while local grammar keeps the sense at guiding rather than literal offering.
topics.reason: The root evidence includes gift and offering pressure, but the local verb selects guidance.

topics.headline: balanced binary with uneven forms
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the binary is balanced by syntax but not flattened in morphology: guidance is direct while misguidance is causative.
topics.reason: The local forms differ: guidance appears in Form I while misguidance appears in Form IV.

topics.headline: guidance completes and extends the binary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees guidance as the positive half of a formulaic binary that continues into later Surah 14 scenes (14:12; 14:21).
topics.reason: The contextual rows link guidance with misguidance, will, and later Surah 14 uses.

words.gloss_range: second open relative object, mirroring the misguidance recipient slot for guidance
words.prose: {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) repeats the same open human slot for guidance that appeared in the misguidance clause. The object grammar stays identical, so the distinction lies in the divine verb and will, not in a different kind of recipient.

topics.headline: same recipient slot for guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guided and misguided recipients are grammatically framed through the same open slot.
topics.reason: The second relative pronoun is object of the guidance verb and repeats the earlier object form in the matching clause.

words.gloss_range: second identical will verb, now tied to guidance, completing the mirrored outcome formula
words.root_gloss_range: root range of willing, determining, and thingness or bringing-about; local Form I repeats divine willing as the invariant term across both outcomes
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَاءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) returns unchanged for the guidance half. The repeated will verb makes divine willing the invariant while the outcome verbs differ, and the omission of criteria remains deliberate. This second occurrence closes the mirrored architecture and points forward to wider Surah 14 will statements.

topics.headline: same will governs guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is governed by the same kind of divine willing as misguidance.
topics.reason: The second will verb matches the first in form and takes its understood object from the guidance clause.

topics.headline: criteria still withheld
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the criteria for selection remain unstated twice, while the root pressure frames will as outcome specification.
topics.reason: The repeated verb gives no rationale, and the root evidence supports determination pressure without changing the local will sense.

topics.headline: repeated formula closes the binary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the two outcome clauses locked into a single repeated formula, with will as the master variable.
topics.reason: The rows identify the exact repeated phrase as the architecture of the misguidance-guidance binary.

words.gloss_range: closing connector that shifts from divine acts to the attribute coda while keeping the relation intact
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa-}}) opens the closing nominal sentence. It can sound resumptive and circumstantial at once: after the outcome binary, the coda declares who the actor is while showing the standing reality under which those acts occur.

topics.headline: transition from acts to attributes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the move from divine action to divine identity without severing the explanation from what came before.
topics.reason: The connector introduces the closing nominal clause after the paired outcome verbs.

words.gloss_range: independent pronoun that re-centers the divine actor as subject of the closing attribute sentence
words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) restates the divine referent as an independent subject before the two attributes. The coda is therefore not a loose pair of titles; it is an identity statement about the same actor who misguides and guides.

topics.headline: detached subject for the attribute seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from verbal agency to stable identity, with both attributes predicated of one subject.
topics.reason: The pronoun is the subject of the closing nominal sentence and anchors both predicates.

words.gloss_range: definite first predicate naming divine might, unassailability, and sovereign power before wisdom
words.root_gloss_range: root range of might, firmness, overcoming, inaccessibility, preciousness, strengthening, and rarity; local epithet selects unassailable divine might as a stable title
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَزِيزُ}} ({{tr:al-ʿazīzu}}) is the first predicate in the seal, so power lands before wisdom in the explanation of the outcome binary. The {{ar:ع ز ز}} ({{tr:ʿ-z-z}}) field gives that power firmness, unassailability, and worth rather than mere force, and the definite title-form makes it a stable divine attribute. Its pairing with the next attribute is formulaic, and it also reconnects this coda to the surah opening (14:1).

topics.headline: power comes first in the seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the coda first explains the preceding acts through sovereign ability.
topics.reason: The word is nominative predicate of the closing pronoun and precedes the wisdom predicate.

topics.headline: might as unassailable firmness and worth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears might as invincible firmness joined to worth, while the local epithet remains the divine title of might.
topics.reason: The root evidence includes firmness, overcoming, value, and rarity; the local definite epithet selects divine might.

topics.headline: formulaic pairing with wisdom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that power is not isolated; the familiar pair immediately binds it to wisdom.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence rows mark the might-wisdom pair as a highly fixed divine seal.

topics.headline: surah-wide authority frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the attribute reconnect this verse to the surah’s broader frame of unassailable divine authority.
topics.reason: The echo row connects this root with the surah opening and later authority claims.

words.gloss_range: definite final predicate naming divine wisdom, judgment, and controlled ordering as the ayah’s closing explanation
words.root_gloss_range: root range of judging, governing, restraining, wisdom, firm construction, and perfected ordering; local epithet selects wise judgment as stable divine title
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَكِيمُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥakīmu}}) is the final landing point of the ayah. It binds wisdom and judgment to the power just named, so the divergent outcomes after clarification are framed as governed rather than arbitrary. The {{ar:ح ك م}} ({{tr:ḥ-k-m}}) field adds restraint and firm construction, making the tight parallel form of the ayah echo its closing attribute.

topics.headline: final wisdom predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the last word resolves the tension by naming wise judgment at the end.
topics.reason: The word functions as the second predicate or tightly bound qualifying partner in the closing nominal sentence.

topics.headline: wisdom as judgment and firm restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears wisdom as governed judgment and restraint, not cleverness or force alone.
topics.reason: The root evidence links wisdom with judgment, arbitration, restraint, and firm construction; the local epithet selects the divine wise title.

topics.headline: formula resolves the outcome binary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole misguidance-guidance allocation sealed by power joined to wisdom rather than by either attribute alone.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and synthesis rows bind the two attributes to the preceding outcome binary.

topics.headline: opening policy lands in wisdom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the initial local-language sending rule is finally framed as a wise communicative structure.
topics.reason: The synthesis row connects the sending-policy opening with the wisdom-governed closure.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The chain أَرْسَلْنَا / رَسُول / بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ / لِيُبَيِّنَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: A dispatched carrier bears a saying through the language already shared by his community, so clarification is a sender-carrier-medium-audience relay rather than an abstract transfer of information.

activation_trace.role: The messenger-and-message image supplies both the carrier and the saying carried through the relay.
Language, speech, news, and message make the people's tongue the relay's shared medium.
The people or community image fixes the audience as the messenger's own social body.
Disclosure by speech or sign supplies the relay's purpose: making the carried meaning accessible.

changed_reading.before: A messenger merely speaks the audience's native language.
changed_reading.after: The message is fitted to an existing communal channel so that sender, carrier, speech, and audience form one intelligible relay.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The purpose clause لِيُبَيِّنَ is immediately followed by the opposed verbs يُضِلُّ and يَهْدِي.
baseline_models.mechanism: Bayān can separate as well as reveal. The clarified field exposes a boundary on which one trajectory veers or disappears while the other is gently directed toward a way.

activation_trace.role: Separation after connection supplies the differentiating edge within clarification.
Appearance and disclosure make that differentiating edge visible.
Disappearance and hiddenness supply one possible trajectory after the field is disclosed.
Gentle indication toward road and truth supplies the opposed directed trajectory.

changed_reading.before: Clarification is neutral explanation followed by unrelated outcomes.
changed_reading.after: Clarification opens a visible differentiating field in which hidden loss and directed movement become opposed trajectories.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The exact repetition مَن يَشَاءُ frames both outcomes, and the ayah closes with ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The paired outcomes remain under one will and are enclosed by prevailing power plus restraint, judgment, and right knowledge. The closure marks governance rather than a failure of the messenger's language.

activation_trace.role: Will attached to an effected thing supplies the symmetric control repeated over both outcomes.
Prevailing force supplies the capacity by which neither outcome escapes divine governance.
Restraint and prevention for repair keep power from reading as undirected force.
Knowledge that reaches the right supplies the discriminating intelligence of the governance.

changed_reading.before: Guidance and misguidance are signs that communication either succeeds or fails.
changed_reading.after: Both outcomes lie inside a powerful but restrained and knowing governance, so linguistic clarity is not identical with compelled uptake.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening purpose chain turns clarification into passage: what is sent enables an emergence from concealment and darkness into illumination and a straight route, under permission.

activation_trace.role: Disclosure by speech or sign anchors the changed mechanism in the focus purpose clause.
Bringing something out of concealment turns verbal disclosure into an enacted extraction.
Light and illumination supply the visible destination of that extraction.
Permission makes the transition authorized rather than an autonomous effect of the speaker.
The straight road converts illumination into a traversable direction.

structural_cues: 14:1 places the sent book, خروج, darkness-to-light motion, permission, and path in one purpose chain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies disclosure, extraction, illumination, permission, and road; I infer that the focus clarification activates a state transition, while the live alternative is that 14:1 describes the book's broader mission without specifying every messenger's speech event.

changed_reading.before: The messenger explains propositions in familiar words.
changed_reading.after: Familiar speech is an authorized extraction medium that moves hearers from a hidden state into visible, traversable direction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The shared language channel can be actively reversed. Hearers obstruct the road, seek its crookedness, and answer manifest proofs by returning and speaking rejection through their own mouths; clarity therefore exposes refusal without coercing assent.

activation_trace.role: Language and speech anchor the mechanism in the focus ayah's shared communicative channel.
Turning away and diverting supply active obstruction rather than passive incomprehension.
Semantic deviation from straightness supplies deliberate distortion of the disclosed way.
Manifest signs make the object of rejection visible rather than obscure.
Non-acceptance and rejection supply the counter-motion applied to the manifest signs.
Opening the mouth in speech locates rejection inside the same bodily channel as communicative clarity.
Interpenetrating alternatives that prevent certainty supply the hearers' declared unsettled state.

structural_cues: 14:3 joins obstruction, path, sought crookedness, and distant error.
14:9 places messengers and manifest signs before a mouth-centered gesture and an explicit declaration of disbelief and doubt.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies obstruction, semantic crookedness, manifest proof, rejection, mouths, and doubt; I infer a reversal of the communicative channel, while the mouth gesture may alternatively accompany rejection without causing it.

changed_reading.before: Using the people's language should remove the decisive obstacle to belief.
changed_reading.after: Shared language makes refusal answerable and visible, but the same channel can carry deliberate distortion, rejection, and doubt.

context_deltas.mechanism: The messenger's relation to 'his people' is not guaranteed harmony. The community can threaten to expel its own messenger or force him back into its followed creed, so local speech places revelation inside a struggle over membership and conformity.

activation_trace.role: The community and kin-group image anchors the belonging that becomes contested.
Shared language places the conflict within, rather than outside, the community's communicative world.
The messengers as carriers of a saying identify the members targeted by the ultimatum.
Passage to the outside supplies threatened removal from the people's land.
Return after departure supplies the demanded reversal back into communal conformity.
A followed creed supplies the social form into which the messengers are ordered to return.

structural_cues: 14:13 gives the disbelieving people a two-part ultimatum to their messengers: leave our land or return to our creed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies shared peoplehood, expulsion, return, and creed; I infer that local-language mission intensifies an internal belonging dispute, while the live alternative is that the ultimatum is political and confessional without a special linguistic mechanism.

changed_reading.before: 'His people' simply identifies the audience best equipped to understand him.
changed_reading.after: 'His people' names an intimate but contested public whose shared speech makes disagreement an internal struggle over land, loyalty, and creed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The ash-and-wind comparison materializes misguidance as loss of retained result. Acquired work becomes residue, violent air scatters it, and its owners cannot recover control over any of it; distant error is dispersal and dispossession as well as a wrong route.

activation_trace.role: Loss of a thing anchors the materialized reading in the focus verb of misguidance.
Ash left by burning supplies a fragile residue for the actors' works.
Wind and moving air supply the carrier that removes the residue.
A violent wind that lightens and scatters things supplies the destructive transport.
Effective capacity and possession are explicitly absent, completing the loss of control.
Seeking and obtaining gain identify what the actors expected their works to retain.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's repeated will becomes concrete in a remove-and-replace operation: God can take the present hearers away and bring a newly originated creation, and that replacement is not difficult for Him.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies willing, removal, new origination, and negated difficulty; I infer that the focus will is effectual and recreative, while the alternative is that the sequence demonstrates general power without specifying how individual guidance outcomes occur.

changed_reading.after: Will is an effective capacity to remove an existing configuration and originate another, with no difficulty constraining the change.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah separates ultimate governance from proximate persuasion. Messenger selection is bestowed by will, compelling proof or force remains permission-bound, social leaders imagine relaying guidance, and the counter-caller finally admits that he only called and hearers answered without coercive authority.

Permission limits the production of compelling proof to divine authorization.
The repeated guidance verbs expose a claimed social relay from leaders to followers.
Loyal succession supplies the follower relation through which guidance was expected to pass.
The denied image of coercive force removes compulsion from the counter-caller's proximate action.
Calling and inclining by speech supply the counter-message's actual intervention.
Answering speech supplies the hearers' uptake of that call.
The self as the thing itself receives blame, locating responsibility at the responding subject.

structural_cues: 14:11 joins divine bestowal, will, lack of independently produced سلطان, and permission.
14:21-22 moves from followers blaming leaders to an explicit no-authority, call-response, blame-yourselves account.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ultimate will, permission-bound proof, social following, denied coercion, call, response, and self-blame; I infer layered causation, while the live alternative is that the focus's divine causation and 14:22's human response remain parallel claims whose precise relation is intentionally unspecified.

changed_reading.before: God directly imposes either guidance or misguidance on isolated recipients.
changed_reading.after: Ultimate divine governance coexists with noncoercive speech, social relays, answering subjects, and proximate responsibility.

context_deltas.mechanism: The locally intelligible message becomes a word that can take root and remain stable or be torn out and lack settlement. The later clause that God stabilizes by the stable saying, misguides, and does what He wills converts the focus pair into a stability-versus-uprooting mechanism.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the two word-tree configurations and then repeats the focus's misguidance and will; I infer that the simile's stability mechanics illuminate the focus pair, while the alternative is that the tree comparison remains an ethical illustration rather than a mechanism for the focus verbs.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final titles unfold as a timed legal sequence. Delay is not heedlessness; warning and an interval for response precede retrospective clarification through inhabited precedents and examples, after which prevailing strength secures the promise to the messengers and punishment follows denial.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because قَوْم in the focus ordinarily names the people, while support, standing, and resurrection are latent branches rather than replacements for that noun. Downstream prose should present it only as a secondary root resonance, never translate قَوْم as 'support system.'

strongest_changes: Local-language clarification became an authorized passage from concealment into visible direction, not mere translation.
Shared speech was shown to permit active rejection without coercion, while ultimate divine governance coexists with social calls and answering subjects.
Misguidance acquired material mechanisms of dispersion, dispossession, uprooting, and loss of settlement.
Repeated divine will became recreative removal and replacement, and the closing titles unfolded as timed restraint, judgment, and promise enforcement.
The final بلاغ sequence extended one messenger's explanation into public warning, recognition, and durable recollection.
summary.what_was_special: The surah repeatedly reintroduced the focus roots inside concrete mechanisms: mouths reject manifest signs, ash loses all recoverable gain, words root or are uprooted, later dwellings make outcomes apparent, and the final message reaches a public. These recurrences kept several readings live without collapsing divine agency, communicative process, and human response into one level.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not resolve the exact causal relation between divine misguidance and the proximate diversion attributed to callers, leaders, people, and idols.
The قَوْم / قيام model may be a productive root resonance rather than a functional sense of the focus noun.
The ه د د warning activation is explicitly packet-supplied but form-distant and should remain exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Clarification separates before guidance selects a course.** `ل س ن` `B006` (language), `ب ي ن` `B001` (separation) and `B005` (disclosing meaning), `ض ل ل` `B002` (becoming hidden), and `ه د ي` `B002` (intended direction) form a sorting mechanism. The later messenger-people disputes show the same intelligible speech producing opposite alignments. The packet supplies disclosure and divergent responses; the inferred arrow is that successful clarification exposes rather than erases volitional division. The ayah reads as language making positions legible before guidance or hiddenness takes effect.

2. **Wisdom operates as restraint within irresistible power.** `ع ز ز` `B002` (overcoming) coexists with `ح ك م` `B001` (restraining to set right) and `B004` (making firm/decisive). Later delay of judgment and fulfillment of promise activate this pairing. I infer that power's assigned role is not immediate compulsion but governed, decisive ordering; the ending qualifies how the preceding divine willing works.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 14:22 unexpectedly clarified the agency boundary: a call can expose a choice without supplying coercive authority; 14:27 then showed clarification stabilizing some while others disappear from the relation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Language is an access channel that crosses separation.** `ل س ن B006` supplies language and spoken expression, and `ب ي ن B005` disclosure by expression or sign; the latter root also retains separation (`ب ي ن B001`) as the condition overcome. The repeated messengers and signs in 14:5 and 14:9 show the channel being offered and then rejected. The packet supplies sender, local language, disclosure, and rejection; I infer that vernacular speech removes an access gap. `لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ` therefore reads as making meaning reachable, not merely restating it.
2. **One activated form of straying is disappearance of the signal.** Alongside directional error (`ض ل ل B001`), `ض ل ل B002` supplies being hidden or disappearing; `ه د ي B001` supplies gentle guidance toward a way. 14:3 supplies active blocking and bending, and 14:9 supplies enacted rejection of messengers. Those human acts are in the packet; I infer the directional arrow by which a rejected signal ceases to orient. `فَيُضِلُّ` can thus be read as allowing the guidance-coordinate to disappear from the rejecter's usable field, without collapsing this into the coexisting route-error reading.
3. **Power is governed by corrective restraint.** `ع ز ز B002` supplies overcoming force, while `ح ك م B001` supplies restraining and turning back in order to set right. Their final pairing follows the opposed outcomes of straying and guidance; 14:6-7 then place rescue, trial, increase, and punishment under announced governance. I infer that wisdom assigns direction to power. `ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ` consequently reads as force whose overcoming capacity is constrained toward ordered correction.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 14:9 was the strongest retrospective activation: the hand-mouth rejection showed how an offered language-channel can be physically closed, making `ض ل ل B002` as disappearance of the guidance-signal newly concrete.

baseline.text: Biz her elçiyi yalnızca kendi halkının diliyle gönderdik ki onlara açıkça anlatsın. Allah dilediğini saptırır, dilediğini doğru yola iletir. O üstündür, hüküm ve hikmet sahibidir.

findings.text: Halkın dili, anlamı erişilebilir kılarak konuşanla dinleyen arasındaki ayrılığı aşan bir erişim kanalıdır.
Açıklama ayrılığı yok etmez; tutumları görünür kılar ve reddedilen yön işaretinin kullanılabilir alandan kaybolmasına kadar varan ayrışmayı açığa çıkarır.
Üstün güç, düzeltici sınırlama ve kararlı düzenleme taşıyan hikmet tarafından yönlendirilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, ortak çekirdeği bir varlığı harekete geçirip göndermek ya da elde tutmayı bırakıp salmak olarak kurar. İnsan, elçi, rüzgar, yağmur ve başka güçler bu işlemin farklı nesneleridir; bunlar ayrı birer çekirdek anlam değildir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, gönderme ve serbest bırakmayı kapsar; yalnızca yavaşlık, süt veya sürü bildiren eşsesli kullanımları kapsamaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanı, canlıyı, doğal gücü ya da başka bir şeyi bulunduğu yerden harekete geçirip bir yöne göndermek; kimi bağlamlarda elde tutmayı bırakıp serbestçe gitmesine izin vermektir.

facets.statement: Temel işlem, bir varlığı durduğu veya tutulduğu konumdan çıkarıp ileri yöneltmektir.
Bir kişi görev veya haber için, rüzgar ve yağmur gibi güçler de etkilerini göstermek üzere gönderilebilir.
Tutmanın karşıtı olarak kullanım, eldeki canlıyı ya da denetlenen gücü salıvermeyi anlatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi güzel ve açık konuşmayı, anlatım açıklığını ve gerekçeyle üstün gelme gücünü aynı yetkinlik alanında birleştirir. Dalın yalnızca organ sahibi olmayı veya bir topluluğun dilini değil, konuşma niteliğini anlatan çerçevesi uygundur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal konuşmanın açıklık, düzgünlük ve ikna gücünü kapsar; konuşma organı ya da belirli bir dil sistemi değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak biçimler doğrudan güzel, açık ve güçlü konuşma yetkinliğini adlandırır; başka yapılara özgü anlamlar eklenmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyin ucunun dil ucuna benzetilmesini ve ayakkabı ya da ayakta görülen ince, hafif uzun biçimi birlikte destekler. Genel biçim ile verilen özel nesne örnekleri ayrıştırıldığında dal çerçevesi kaynağa uygundur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek, dil ucuna benzeyen biçimdir; ayakkabı ucu ve ince, hafif uzun ayak bu biçimin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel biçim bildiren yalın kullanım ile ayakkabı ve ayağa bağlı özel kullanımlar ayrı tutulur; özel örnekler bütün nesnelere yayılmaz.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar dil ucuna benzeyen ince ve uzunca biçimde birleşir; ayakkabının ön ucu ve ayağın hafif uzun, ince yapısı bu biçimin başlıca özel örnekleridir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dil ve konuşma anlamları, sözcük ya da haber uzantıları ve topluluğa veya övgüye bağlı özel yapılar birbirine karıştırılmadan tanımlanır.

concept_map.definition: Bir topluluğun kullandığı dil sistemi veya bu sistemle ortaya konan konuşmadır. Bu çekirdekten söz, haber ya da ileti; topluluk adına konuşan kişi; insanlar arasında dolaşan övgü ve dillerle ses renkleri arasındaki ayrılık anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir topluluğun kullandığı dil sistemi ve o sistemle gerçekleşen konuşmadır.
Konuşma ürününden hareketle söz, sözcük, haber veya ileti anlamına uzanır.
Topluluk adına konuşan kişi, özel bir yapıda topluluğun sesi olarak adlandırılır.
İnsanların biri hakkında söyledikleri, özellikle dolaşan övgü, başka bir özel yapıda anlatılır.
Çoğul kullanım, dillerin ve konuşma seslerinin çeşitliliğini gösterebilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir kişinin kendi deve yavrusunu başkasına ödünç vermesini, yavrunun dişi deveden süt tatmasını, süt inince uzaklaştırılmasını ve yavrusuz dişi devenin bu işlemdeki adını açıkça sıralar. Dal çerçevesi bu teknik süreci doğru korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: İşlem ödünç yavru, sütü indirilecek dişi deve, sütü tattırma ve ardından yavruyu uzaklaştırma aşamalarının tümünü gerektirir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın terimler bu özel hayvancılık işlemini ve işlemdeki yavrusuz dişi deveyi adlandırır; genel süt verme veya sağma anlamına genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin deve yavrusunu, başkasının dişi devesinin sütünü indirtmek üzere ödünç vermesi; yavrunun sütten diliyle tatmasından ve süt inmesinden sonra uzaklaştırılması işlemidir. İşlemde yavru verilen yavrusuz dişi deve de özel olarak adlandırılır.

facets.statement: Bir kişi kendi deve yavrusunu, başka birinin dişi devesinin sütünü indirtmek için ödünç verir.
Yavru sütten diliyle tadar; dişi devenin sütü inince yavru ondan uzaklaştırılır.
Bu işlemde yavru verilen yavrusuz dişi deve özel bir adla anılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sözcüğün yalancı anlamında aktarıldığını gösterir, ancak aynı toplu tanıklık içinde bu kullanımın tanınmadığını bildiren açık bir itiraz da vardır. Anlam dalı korunabilir, fakat kullanımın tartışmalı olduğu her tanımda görünür kalmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca tartışmalı biçimde yalancı diye nitelenen kişiyi kapsar; dil ucu kesilmiş kişi ve genel güzel konuşan kişi ayrı anlamlardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın biçimin yalancı kişi anlamı, tanıklık üzerindeki itirazla birlikte verilir; daha genel yalan veya söz söyleme anlamları eklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Yalan söyleyen kişiyi niteleyen, sözlüklerde aktarılmış olmakla birlikte kullanımının tanınırlığına açıkça itiraz edilmiş bir addır.

facets.statement: Yalan söyleyen kişiyi, yani yalancıyı niteler.
Kullanım bazı aktarımlarda kabul edilirken aynı kaynak kümesinde onu tanımadığını bildiren bir itiraz bulunur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Sözcük yalancı diye açıklanır; ancak aynı aktarım kümesinde bu kullanımı tanımadığını bildiren açık bir itiraz da yer alır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalan söyleyen kişiyi gösteren anlamsal karşılıktır; kaynak kullanımının tartışmalı olduğu ayrıca belirtilmelidir.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin yalan söyleyen biri olarak nitelenmesini korur.
error_profile.collision: Tek başına karşılık, kaynak biçimin tanınırlığına yönelik itirazı göstermez; bu bilgi uygulama notunda korunur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tartışmalı kaynak biçimin kişi anlamını açıklamak gerektiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yalan söyleyen kişi çekirdeğini açıkça verir.
error_profile.collision: Karşılık tek başına tanıklığın tartışmalı olduğunu bildirmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yalancı kişi anlamındaki tek biçimdir ve bu kullanımın tanınırlığı tartışmalıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yalancı kişi yanında yalan söyleme eylemini ve uydurulmuş sözü de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da yalan söyleyen kişiyi adlandırabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Kişi anlamında büyük ölçüde örtüşürler; odak dal tartışmalı tek kişi adıdır, komşu dal ise eylem ve uydurma söz alanına da uzanır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yalnızca yalan söyleyen kişiyi niteleyen tartışmalı bir biçimdir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yalanın kendisini, büyük yalanı, yalan söyleyen kişiyi ve insanları gerçekten saptırmayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Yalan söyleyen kişi iki dalın kesişim alanıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal kişi niteliğiyle sınırlıdır; komşu dal yalanın türünü, eylemini ve saptırıcı etkisini de kapsayan daha geniş bir alandır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yalan söyleme alışkanlığı veya niteliği bulunan kişiyi genel olarak gösterir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Suçsuz bir kişiye yapmadığı bir şeyi yükleyen, şaşırtıcı ve çirkin bir yalanı gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal gerçek dışı söz söyleme alanındadır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal yalancı kişiyi adlandırır; komşu dal belirli bir mağdura yönelen ağır, uydurma suçlamayı tanımlar.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; yalancı kişiyle en yakın örtüşen dal, daha geniş yalan alanı ve ağır uydurma suçlama dalı yayımlandı.
